This species is not included in the FCIN12 Table 1a dataset used by VERA. Please select a proxy species from the full FCIN12 list. The proxy affects the FCIN12 age estimate only.
How proxy selection works (FCIN12)
FCIN12 (White, 1998) requires a proxy species when the selected tree species is not listed in Table 1a. VERA will apply the selected proxy species’ Table 1a values together with the chosen growth context. OpenBARD continues to use the actual selected species/genus where suitable reference data are available; Integrate+ habitat interpretation uses the actual species and DBH where its reference data support that comparison.

Veteranisation features / Veteran Architecture Index (VAI) Condition route

Record how far each veteran structure has developed. Established or Advanced evidence in at least one qualifying feature supports Gate 2.

Veteran Architecture Index (VAI) — restructuring gate

How the veteran structure gate works
VAI reads the structural history of the tree: retrenchment, reiteration, functional reorganisation, recovery after failure or management, decay with adaptive living response, and rooting strategies that sustain an old structure. Emerging and Progressing observations provide life-history context; Established and Advanced observations provide the gate evidence. Heartwood decay and aerial roots contribute where they form part of an established veteranisation process. TreMs are recorded separately as habitat evidence.
Professional judgement
Professional judgement is central. Your experience remains invaluable when interpreting the tree’s veteran character, survival history and any uncertainty.

Tree-related microhabitats / habitat evidence

Counts (0–10). Confirm the catalogue threshold where needed. VERA records the exact TreM identity, scale/threshold and replacement class; Integrate+ is used only to interpret habitat rarity for comparable species and actual DBH where the data support it.
Any recorded TreM is treated as assessed. If none are recorded, choose “Assessment complete” before VERA treats zero TreMs as a real observation rather than missing data.
Cavities & hollows (1–15)

Data & backup
Each assessment is stored under the current project UUID in the browser database. Form drafts auto-save. Assessment photographs are stored separately from the form record so normal autosave does not repeatedly rewrite image data. JSON backup is the restorable archive; CSV is the GIS/interchange export.
How this assessment is assembled
VERA considers the tree as an individual. ATF identifies ancient status; White/FCIN12 interprets maturity, indicative age and developmental time; VAI records established veteran restructuring; OpenBARD describes species-relative size/form; Integrate+ interprets the TreM assemblage; replacement evidence describes recreation difficulty. Heritage and cultural evidence record the human story within the biography.

New VERA project

Methods & sources
VERA principle: VERA reconstructs the tree biography from distinct evidence sources. ATF identifies ancient trees; White/FCIN12 interprets maturity, indicative age and developmental time; VAI records established veteran restructuring; OpenBARD reports species-relative physical size/form; Integrate+ interprets TreM richness/occurrence rarity around the subject's actual DBH; TreM replacement classes describe recreation difficulty; heritage and cultural selections record the human story.

Sources: White, J. (1998), Estimating the Age of Large and Veteran Trees in Britain (FCIN12); OpenBARD / Handbook of UK Urban Tree Allometric Equations and Size Characteristics; Ancient Tree Forum girth guidance; Lonsdale (2013); Bütler et al. (2024) Tree-related Microhabitats field guide; Integrate+ tree-level TreM reference data.

Integrate+ data scope: the current tree-level host dataset provides species, DBH and TreM richness/count. Exact TreM codes and global frequencies are shown separately as composition evidence; species-specific code percentiles are reserved for host-by-code data when that evidence is available.
Outputs are indicative diagnostic estimates and should be interpreted by a competent arboricultural professional.
